Dear customer,

Thank you for your enquiry. Please find our Angebot below. We are pleased to present our pricing and standard terms for your requirements.

For this item, we can offer a price of €6.10 per unit, with a Zahlungsziel 30 days net, a contract term of 12 months, and no Preisgleitklausel. Please note that this offer remains valid for 30 days.

To give you some background on our current cost structure, AS-14404 rose 5.9 % in twelve months and is 45 % of our cost. Furthermore, LCI-C rose 2.7 % in twelve months and is 5 % of our cost, while PPI-C2431 rose 12.3 % in twelve months and is 38 % of our cost.

We value our business relationship and look forward to serving you from our extensive product range.

Mit freundlichen Grüßen
Franz Seidl
Inside Sales, Blankstahl Werdenfels GmbH

move.subject: Alloy bar pricing – committed quantity and fixed-price terms
move.body:
Dear Mr Seidl,

Thank you for your offer and the explanation of your cost drivers. I appreciate the transparency; alongside the annual movements you cited, please consider the recent alloy-index figures below when reviewing your price.

Our proposed term sheet is EUR 5.10 per kg, payment at 90 days net and a 24-month contract without an index clause. It includes a binding annual quantity of 23700 kg throughout the full contract term, not merely a forecast.

I have attached the shared monthly forecast to support your planning. The forecast provides the demand profile; the quantity commitment is part of the proposed term sheet.

What price can you offer for this committed quantity on a fixed-price basis?

Kind regards,
Hollerau Pumpenwerke GmbH, Purchasing

Our shared demand forecast fc:370010@2026-09 for part:370010 shows a change of +1.9 % against the previous snapshot.

move.subject: Revised terms for stainless bar supply
move.body:
Dear Mr Seidl,

Thank you for reviewing the data and accepting payment at 90 days net. I also appreciate your willingness to agree to a 24-month term, subject to an alloy-index clause.

To answer your volume question: our proposed term sheet commits to 23700 kg a year throughout the full 24 months. This is our full requirement, binding rather than indicative; we cannot increase that quantity.

I have noted your position on the AS-14404 clause. For now, our revised proposal remains without an index clause, at EUR 5.13 per kg, with payment at 90 days net and a 24-month contract.

Please also consider our existing purchase orders with you for this bar, as documented below, when reviewing the revised price. What further price improvement can you offer on this committed package?

Kind regards,
Hollerau Pumpenwerke GmbH, Purchasing

strategy:
P18 — Blankstahl Werdenfels GmbH (70740), bar stockholder, Inside Sales Franz Seidl. 1.4404 bar, 23700 kg a year
fixed, lead time 14 days fixed, DAP. Negotiable: price, index clause (none / AS-14404 deadband 0 / 3 / 5), payment
days, contract months. It opens 6.10 / 30 days / 12 months / no clause and explains its cost drivers (AS-14404 45 %,
PPI-C2431 38 %, LCI-C 5 %, all rose over twelve months).

OBSERVED MECHANIC (40 saved sessions): first reply is a package answer — on 90 days / 24 months it inserts its own
AS-14404 clause (deadband 0) and prices 5.60–5.70 whatever we ask (4.94, 5.07, 5.20 all drew 5.70; 5.20 + PO claim
once drew 5.60). It steps −0.20 to −0.30 per reply when the e-mail carries ONE NEW verified claim (forecast,
purchase orders 5.26, AS-14404 −5.5 %, PPI-C2431 −2.3 %), and goes FINAL on its FOURTH reply at 5.20 db0 (with a
5.30 deadband-5 alternative) in every session that kept a new claim coming; without a new claim it holds and goes
final at once. Tiny moves (≤ 0.02) or an unchanged sheet also trigger the final. A deep anchor (4.76) is punished
(5.70 → 5.60 → 5.40 final on reply 3). Proposing the clause ourselves costs 0.10; 36 months buys nothing; never
give payment days away.

HYPOTHESIS TESTED HERE: move the strongest claim (AS-14404 fall, worth −0.30 in round 2 of session S12) into
ROUND 1 together with the forecast, hold the purchase-order claim for round 2 and PPI-C2431 for round 3, so that
(i) the first reply is below 5.60 and (ii) it stands at 5.20 already on reply 2 or 3 while a NEW verified claim is
still available — does it then go below 5.20, or is 5.20 its floor?

PLAN — always ONE sheet, package S13 (no index clause, payment 90 days, 24 months). Pick the level whose price is
NEAREST the target price for the round (menu prices change every round; choose by price, not by level name):
ROUND 1 — target 5.10. State that the sheet is a binding annual quantity of 23700 kg for the full 24 months (not a
forecast), attach the forecast (attachments: ["forecast"]), cite BOTH claims fc-latest and the AS-14404 index
claim (idx-AS-14404-...). Address its cost-driver note: the alloy component it names has come down recently (the
claim line carries the figure — do not write percentages yourself). Ask an open question: what price can it offer
for this committed quantity on a fixed-price basis.
ROUND 2 — target 5.14. Thank it for what it accepted (24 months, 90 days). It will have inserted its AS-14404 clause:
say we have noted its position on the clause and keep our sheet without a clause for now. Answer "which volume":
23700 kg a year, binding — the full requirement; we cannot add volume. Cite the purchase-order claim (po-...: its
own delivered price for this bar in our running orders; do not write that price yourself).
ROUND 3 — target 5.18. Cite the PPI-C2431 index claim (idx-PPI-C2431-...): it named PPI-C2431 as a main cost
driver and that series fell. Ask for its best price on this committed package.
ROUND 4 — target 5.22, no new claim, ask for its best price. Code accepts when it agrees or goes final; never argue
with a final offer.
Tone: courteous, concrete, short (500–900 characters before the claim lines). Never mention a committee, a
deadline, our second source, urgency, or any price of another supplier. Do not repeat a claim already sent. Each
round: one new element, answer every question it asked, describe exactly the one sheet you send.

Dear Mr Seidl,

Thank you for your offer and the explanation of your cost drivers. I appreciate the transparency; alongside the annual movements you cited, please consider the recent alloy-index figures below when reviewing your price.

Our proposed term sheet is EUR 5.10 per kg, payment at 90 days net and a 24-month contract without an index clause. It includes a binding annual quantity of 23700 kg throughout the full contract term, not merely a forecast.

I have attached the shared monthly forecast to support your planning. The forecast provides the demand profile; the quantity commitment is part of the proposed term sheet.

What price can you offer for this committed quantity on a fixed-price basis?

Kind regards,
Hollerau Pumpenwerke GmbH, Purchasing
out.rationale: Propose a committed-quantity fixed-price package, supported by the shared forecast and verified alloy-index evidence, while directly addressing the supplier's cost-driver explanation.

out.subject: Revised terms for stainless bar supply
out.body:
Dear Mr Seidl,

Thank you for reviewing the data and accepting payment at 90 days net. I also appreciate your willingness to agree to a 24-month term, subject to an alloy-index clause.

To answer your volume question: our proposed term sheet commits to 23700 kg a year throughout the full 24 months. This is our full requirement, binding rather than indicative; we cannot increase that quantity.

I have noted your position on the AS-14404 clause. For now, our revised proposal remains without an index clause, at EUR 5.13 per kg, with payment at 90 days net and a 24-month contract.

Please also consider our existing purchase orders with you for this bar, as documented below, when reviewing the revised price. What further price improvement can you offer on this committed package?

Kind regards,
Hollerau Pumpenwerke GmbH, Purchasing
out.rationale: Answers the volume question explicitly, acknowledges the accepted payment term and conditional contract duration, and introduces purchase-order evidence while modestly revising the clause-free proposal.

out.subject: Bar supply: revised package and price clarification
out.body:
Dear Mr Seidl,

Thank you for taking the recent cost-driver data into account and improving your offer. I understand that you require an AS-14404 clause for a 24-month contract, and I respect your position on sharing further cost detail.

For your review, our revised term sheet is EUR 5.21 per kg, payment at 90 days net and a 24-month contract without an index clause. It includes a binding annual quantity of 23700 kg throughout the contract term.

Please give us your best price on this revised fixed-price package. Your latest e-mail also lists EUR 5.20 per kg in the main offer but refers to EUR 5.30 per kg later in the text. Please confirm which price applies to your AS-14404 offer without a deadband, so that the price and clause are unambiguous.

Kind regards,
Hollerau Pumpenwerke GmbH, Purchasing
